topics.title: Design a Chess Game
topics.summary: A lighter but complete chess design: board, polymorphic pieces with move rules, turn management, capture and check detection, with notes on castling and en passant.
keyPoints: Each piece subclass overrides canMove with its geometry; shared helpers handle straight and diagonal sliding.
The board validates path clearance for sliding pieces; knights skip the path check.
Game validation pipeline: piece exists, correct turn, not capturing own piece, geometry, no self-check.
Self-check is detected by simulating the move, testing if the king is attacked, then reverting.
Checkmate = in check with no legal moves; stalemate = not in check with no legal moves.
Moves are Command-like records in a history stack for undo, en passant and notation.
Scope clearly: castling, en passant and promotion are typical extensions, not P0.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you avoid a giant switch on piece type?
interviewQuestions.a: Make `Piece` abstract with an abstract `canMove(board, from, to)` and let each subclass implement its geometry - runtime polymorphism. Shared helpers in the base class (`straight`, `diagonal`) avoid duplication, so `Queen` is just `straight || diagonal`. The game calls `piece.canMove(...)` without knowing the type. Adding a fairy piece (say, an Archbishop combining bishop and knight) means one new class, satisfying the Open/Closed Principle.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you detect that a move leaves the king in check?
interviewQuestions.a: Temporarily apply the move on the board, find the mover's king, and check whether any opponent piece can move to that square (`isAttacked`), then restore the original pieces. If the king is attacked, the move is illegal. This handles pinned pieces and moving the king into check uniformly. For efficiency, engines compute attack maps incrementally, but simulate-and-revert is the clear and correct approach for an interview.

Track whether the king and each rook have moved (a `hasMoved` flag updated on every move, restored on undo). Castling is legal when neither has moved, the squares between them are empty, the king is not currently in check, and the squares the king passes through and lands on are not attacked. The move relocates both king and rook, so it is best modelled as a special `Move` subtype (`CastleMove`) whose execute and undo handle both pieces.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you support undo in chess?
interviewQuestions.a: Store each executed move as an object containing from, to, the moving piece, the captured piece, and any special-state changes (castling rights, en passant square, promotion piece, hasMoved flags). Push it onto a history stack. Undo pops the last move and restores everything it recorded, then switches the turn back. This is the Command pattern; the same history also generates PGN notation and supports replay.

topics.title: Design a Hotel Booking System
topics.summary: Design a hotel reservation system with room types, date-range availability, overlap-safe booking, pricing strategies and cancellation.
keyPoints: Use half-open date ranges [checkIn, checkOut); ranges overlap iff s1 < e2 and s2 < e1.
Keep bookings per room in a TreeMap keyed by check-in for O(log n) overlap checks via lowerEntry.
Lock per room so bookings for different rooms proceed concurrently without double booking.
Pricing and cancellation refunds are Strategies; weekend surcharges computed per night.
Booking lifecycle transitions are guarded: CONFIRMED -> CHECKED_IN -> CHECKED_OUT or CANCELLED.
DateRange as an immutable record encapsulates validation and overlap logic.
At scale, OTAs track per-date inventory counts per room type and enforce uniqueness in the database.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you check if a room is available for a date range efficiently?
interviewQuestions.a: Represent stays as half-open intervals. Store each room's bookings in a `TreeMap` keyed by check-in date. Because bookings of one room never overlap each other, the only booking that can conflict with a new range is the one with the greatest check-in strictly before the new check-out (`lowerEntry(newEnd)`); if its check-out is after the new check-in, there is a conflict. That is O(log n) per room instead of a linear scan.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you prevent two guests from booking the same room for overlapping dates at the same time?
interviewQuestions.a: Make check-and-insert atomic per room. In memory I synchronize on that room's booking map, so concurrent requests for the same room serialize while different rooms proceed in parallel. In a database, model per-night rows (`room_id, date`) with a unique constraint so the second insert fails, or use per-date inventory counts with optimistic locking (`UPDATE ... SET available = available - 1 WHERE available > 0 AND version = ?`).

A hotel stay naturally occupies nights from check-in up to, but not including, the check-out date. With `[start, end)`, one guest checking out on the 12th and another checking in on the 12th do not overlap, which is the correct business behaviour. Night counts become `end - start` without off-by-one errors, and the overlap condition `s1 < e2 && s2 < e1` stays simple.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you support different cancellation policies per rate plan?
interviewQuestions.a: Model `CancellationPolicy` as a strategy with `refund(booking, today)`: fully refundable until 7 days before, 50% until 2 days, non-refundable, and so on. Attach the chosen policy to each booking at booking time (its rate plan) so later policy changes do not affect existing reservations. The cancellation flow simply calls `booking.policy().refund(...)`, and new policies are just new classes.

topics.title: Design a Pub-Sub Message Queue
topics.summary: Build a Kafka-inspired in-memory message queue with topics, multiple subscribers, per-subscriber offsets, async consumer workers and replay.
keyPoints: Store messages in an append-only topic log; subscribers keep independent offsets (Kafka model).
Fan-out is free: every subscriber reads the same log at its own pace, and offsets enable replay.
Each subscription has a worker that waits when caught up and is notified on publish (guarded wait in a loop).
Publishing is O(1) and never blocks on slow consumers.
Broker is a Facade over topics, handlers and workers; Observer/Pub-Sub decouples producers and consumers.
Failure handling: retry with backoff, then dead-letter topic; commit the offset after successful processing for at-least-once.
Consumer groups and partitions are the standard scaling extensions.

interviewQuestions.q: Why use offsets instead of deleting messages after delivery?
interviewQuestions.a: With an append-only log and per-subscriber offsets, each subscriber progresses independently: a slow email service does not delay analytics, and neither blocks the publisher. Messages are written once regardless of subscriber count (no per-subscriber copies). Replay becomes trivial - reset the offset - which is invaluable for recovering from bugs or onboarding a new consumer. Retention policies then delete old messages by time or size rather than on consumption. This is exactly Kafka's design.

interviewQuestions.q: How do you guarantee ordering and at-least-once delivery?
interviewQuestions.a: Ordering per subscriber comes from a single worker processing messages sequentially by offset. For at-least-once, the offset is committed only after `consume` succeeds; if the consumer crashes mid-processing, it restarts from the last committed offset and may see a message twice, so consumers must be idempotent (dedupe by message id). At-most-once commits before processing. Exactly-once needs idempotent consumers plus transactional offset commits.

interviewQuestions.q: How would you implement consumer groups?
interviewQuestions.a: A consumer group is a set of subscribers that share the work: each message goes to only one member. Either keep one shared offset per group and let members atomically claim the next offset (`getAndIncrement`), which loses strict ordering, or split the topic into partitions and assign each partition to exactly one member, which preserves per-partition order. Rebalancing reassigns partitions when members join or leave.

interviewQuestions.q: What happens if a subscriber keeps failing on a message?
interviewQuestions.a: It must not block the subscriber forever (a poison message). Retry a bounded number of times with exponential backoff; if it still fails, publish the message plus error details to a dead-letter topic and advance the offset. Operators can inspect the dead-letter topic and replay messages after a fix. My demo simply logs and skips; a `RetryPolicy` strategy would make this configurable per subscriber.
